(1) we introduce the first deep learning framework that accounts for the fact that some domains may need to go through more operations (more computations) than others; (2) we show that our framework outperforms the state-of-the-art in unsupervised domain adaption by a large margin, on both the Office31 and OfficeHome datasets; and (3) we show how the framework can be extended to handle multiple domains, and we show that it outperforms the current state-of

(a) the proposed method is effective in unsupervised domain adaption, (b) it is simple to implement, (c) it is easy to extend to more than two domains, (d) it can be combined with other state-of-the-art methods to further improve the performance, (e) it does not require any domain-specific training data, and (f) it is robust to the choice of hyper-parameters

1) a single domain-adaptive network can be used for multiple source-target domain adaptation problems; 2) a single network can be adapted to multiple source-target domains by training it on multiple source-target domain pairs; 3) a single network trained on multiple source-target domains can be further fine-tuned to adapt to new source-target domain pairs.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions. How can we adapt the network architecture to the specific characteristics of each domain? How can we learn a shared feature space that is effective for classification across all domains?
the development of novel neural network architectures for unsupervised domain adaption.
two questions: (1) how to learn a common representation of different domains? and (2) how to learn domain-specific representations?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in general, the use of deep learning methods for the purpose of unsupervised domain adaption is not recommended, and that, if it is used, it must be used in a very careful way.
the use of domain adaptation techniques is a good way to reduce the domain gap between source and target data and improve classification performance.
the proposed framework can be used to learn a feature extractor from the target domain that is able to perform well in the source domain as well, while the opposite does not happen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel deep network architecture, called Domain Adaptive Multibranch Network (DAMNet), which is able to handle the complexity of the data in each of the different domains.
we propose a deep learning framework that can learn multiple feature representations from different domains, and then combine them to produce a single, common feature representation for recognition.
we introduce an adaptive architecture for domain adaptation, which we call Domain Adaptive Multibranch Network (DAMN).
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in contrast to existing domain adaptation methods, our framework can be applied to any deep learning architecture and it is not constrained to a particular type of network.
a single network architecture is not sufficient to deal with all domains.
, in contrast to previous works that assume that all domains are processed in the same manner, we show that this is not always the case.
